key_insight: Longitudinal ribs generate counter-rotating secondary vortices and strongly alter near-wall turbulence, with rectangular ribs producing a larger roughness effect while triangular ribs intensify near-wall TKE production.
engineering_relevance: Rib shape and spacing can be tuned to control drag, wall shear, and mixing in channel flows, which is useful for heat-transfer surfaces and roughness design.
method: Large Eddy Simulation (LES) of channel flow at friction Reynolds number 220.
Compared rectangular and triangular surface-mounted longitudinal ribs with aspect ratio W/h = 2 and spacing S = 0.6H.
Analyzed secondary vortices, wall shear stress, Reynolds stresses, and turbulence production/dissipation across the wall-normal direction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two counter-rotating vortices between adjacent ribs in both cases, a higher roughness function for rectangular ribs, and distinct wall-shear-stress and Reynolds-stress profiles.
watch_item: Results are from a single Reynolds number and a specific rib geometry, so broader design conclusions may require additional parameter sweeps and validation.
paper_title: Secondary Flows and Near-Wall Turbulence in Channel Flow with Longitudinal Ribs
